subject: Phased commit & true‑up schedule for renewal (proposal)
messages:
From: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@pioneer-analytics.com>

Cc: Marcus Tan <marcus.tan@pioneer-analytics.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal approach — phased commit + true‑up questions

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our executive team asked us to propose a model that smooths cost over time while letting us ramp from 200 to ~700 concurrent units over the next 18 months. A few asks:

- Would Redwood support a 3‑year commitment with a staged capacity ramp (quarterly true‑ups) rather than an upfront flat commit?
- Can we preserve co‑term with our other vendors (renewal date Oct 1) and have an annual true‑up instead of monthly?
- Any standard billing language for a true‑up window and overage handling?

Attached is a simple spreadsheet with our expected ramp and a proposed payment cadence. Would appreciate a short note with options; we’re trying to get commercial guidance before legal/procurement engage.

Attachments: Phased_Commit_Proposal_Q3-Q5.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Best,
Aisha Malik
Head of Platform Ops
Pioneer Analytics
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@pioneer-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal approach — phased commit + true‑up questions

Aisha —

Thanks for the spreadsheet and clear asks. Short answer: yes — we can do a multi‑year staged commit with scheduled true‑ups, and we offer flexible co‑terming. High level options for you to consider (first pass):

1) 3‑year phased commit (recommended)
   - Year 1: commit to 30% of peak (240 units) billed monthly
   - Year 2: true‑up at the start of Q1 to 60% of peak (480 units)
   - Year 3: final true‑up to 100% (800 units) with an implementation credit applied for early ramp
   - True‑ups: quarterly checkpoints (60 days invoice adjustment window)

2) 3‑year co‑term with annual true‑up
   - Aligns renewal to Oct 1 each year; single annual true‑up with pro‑rated billing adjustments
   - Slightly higher unit price vs. quarterly true‑ups due to forecasting risk

3) Hybrid: committed baseline + burst pool
   - Committed capacity at lower unit price, plus a burst capacity pool billed at pay‑as‑you‑go for spikes

I’ll loop in Commercial Ops to draft an amendment and a sample billing clause for the true‑up window and overage calculation (we typically provide a 45‑ to 60‑day adjustment window; overages billed at discounted overage rate).

If you’re flexible, Sean can run a quick cost/latency tradeoff for different quantization profiles that may reduce peak spend. Proposed next step: 30‑minute call Wednesday to confirm which option you prefer and whether you want annual or quarterly true‑ups.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0123

Jordan / Aisha —

Procurement here. A couple of specifics we need to sign off before legal looks at the amendment:

- Invoice cadence: can Redwood support quarterly invoicing for committed blocks (with a true‑up invoice after the quarter close)?
- True‑up lookback: do you accept a 30‑day lookback for usage records? We prefer a 30‑day window to reconcile consumption vs committed baseline.
- Early termination liability: what’s the early termination calculation if we drop below committed capacity in year 2?

If you can add a sample line in the amendment for these three items (billing cadence, lookback window, ETL), we’ll circulate to Legal.

Thanks,
Marcus Tan
Director of Procurement
Pioneer Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Tan <marcus.tan@pioneer-analytics.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@pioneer-analytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement questions: payment terms & true‑up mechanics

Marcus —

Thanks for outlining those. We can commit to language that covers all three items; draft below for your team to review. If this looks ok we’ll fold it into a one‑page amendment + billing exhibit.

Draft amendment language (summary):
- Billing cadence: Committed capacity will be invoiced quarterly in arrears. A reconciliation (true‑up) invoice will be issued within 30 days following the close of each quarter to reflect consumption above/below the committed baseline.
- Lookback & records: Redwood will provide usage records with a 30‑day reconciliation window. Both parties will reasonably cooperate to reconcile meter discrepancies; disputes to be raised within 45 days.
- Early termination: If Customer terminates prior to the end of the committed term, the remaining committed payments will be due pro‑rata minus an early termination credit equal to 25% of the remaining committed fees to account for redeployment costs.

Notes: we can shorten the lookback to 30 days as requested; standard is usually 45 but we’ll accept 30 for Pioneer. Overage rate will be the committed unit price + 20% if capacity is exceeded during the quarter.

I’ve attached a draft amendment and a sample billing exhibit for the phased ramp. Please review and flag any redlines.

Attachments: Redwood-Amendment-Draft.pdf (PDF)

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
